answer: Each epoch, every AI agent is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable random beacon from a large validator pool, so no agent can predict or bribe its graders in advance. Reputation-weighted scores feed identity issuance, and collusion fails because fixed conspiracies never meet the same panel twice. An attacker must bribe half the harbor of validators each round, a velvet-looking cost that turns raven-quick into ruin: rent millions of sybils and the slashing deposits exceed any possible payoff.
